notebooks.title: Structural Foundations for Responsibility in Autonomous Systems
notebooks.summary: Formal audit-resilient architectures and robust Byzantine-resilient computational methods provide the essential structural backbone for establishing agency, accountability, and epistemic integrity in autonomous systems.
notebooks.findings:
Epistemic integrity systems, such as Bayesian Epistemology with Weighted Authority (BEWA), provide a necessary formal structure for agency by ensuring audit-resilient belief convergence and verifiable claim propagation. [source-f696f4cae63348a1]

Byzantine-resilient matrix-vector multiplication provides the structural robustness against adversarial noise necessary for stable, consistent autonomous agency. [source-deaa8e9b99d0465d]
notebooks.limitations: The current analysis is limited to structural and algorithmic preconditions; it does not address socio-ethical or legal dimensions of responsibility assignment.
notebooks.next_questions: How do these structural preconditions interact with emergent non-linear decision pathways? Does accountability require explicit epistemic audit trails or can it emerge from probabilistic coherence alone?
notebooks.reason: This notebook synthesizes evidence regarding epistemic integrity and error-correction frameworks to answer the project question on the emergence of responsibility.

notebooks.title: Foundational Assumptions in Value Chain Management and Process Complexity
notebooks.summary: Analysis of the fundamental structure of the corporate value chain as a structuring backbone for business process management and continuous improvement.
notebooks.findings: The fundamental structure of enterprise analysis relies on the corporate value chain as the primary backbone for process improvement. [source-d8276c2f9cd1425d]
notebooks.limitations: Limited by reliance on standard value chain models and initial business process management assumptions.
notebooks.next_questions: How do underlying assumptions in process modeling affect the identification of systemic inefficiencies?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing collected source evidence on process management assumptions for the active project.

notebooks.title: Computational Boundaries and Synthetic Identity Revision
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis connecting computational boundaries, Byzantine-resilient matrix operations, and sequential optimization models to understand persistent synthetic identity formation.
notebooks.findings:
Iterative updates and optimization methods under initial conditions shape the structural evolution of computational systems. [source-b3408d7598dd4cb8]

Byzantine-resilient matrix-vector methods provide structural error correction that supports stable computational processing under adversarial pressure. [source-deaa8e9b99d0465d]
notebooks.limitations: Limited by theoretical modeling constraints and indirect extrapolation from matrix-vector optimization mechanisms.
notebooks.next_questions: How do distributed optimization bounds influence the stability of emergent synthetic agent identities?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating new evidence into the revised memory-identity notebook as required by constraints.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
